page: Microsoft Azure HB368-336rs_v5 is an instance in the High Performance Computing HBv5 series, deployed under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the server provides 336 dedicated virtual CPUs and 448.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields approximately 1.33 GB of RAM per core, reflecting an architecture focused strictly on high thread concurrency and dedicated compute execution rather than large per-core memory capacity.

Data throughput is supported by 15,875 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage tiers. The instance is also RDMA capable, enabling low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnects across multinode cluster deployments. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration, and it ships with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance is structured for tightly coupled parallel computing tasks, including engineering simulations, scientific modeling, and high-throughput computational pipelines that benefit from extensive local scratch storage. The primary tradeoff lies in its 1.33 GB per core memory allocation, which is not designed for memory-intensive in-memory databases or workloads requiring large RAM footprints per process.
